previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with weakness and confusion due to malignant hypercalcemia in the setting of relapsed refractory multiple myeloma. He had recently received pamidronate, so he was treated with IV fluids and nasal calcitonin instead. His hospital course was complicated by steroid-induced hyperglycemia requiring an insulin drip and subsequent insulin regimen adjustment, with glargine increased to 35 units nightly. His renal function fluctuated but stabilized with careful fluid management. He reported dyspnea on exertion, but imaging and V/Q scan ruled out pulmonary embolism or significant fluid overload; a pharmacologic stress test was arranged outpatient to evaluate for cardiac causes. He remained on oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis and continued chemotherapy with bortezomib and dexamethasone. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor blood glucose four times daily, follow up with endocrinology and oncology, and schedule a cardiac stress test.

Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF SUMMARY
=============
Mr. ___ is a ___ with relapsed refractory multiple myeloma s/p 
autologous transplant (___) and several chemotherapy 
regimens, h/o bilateral PEs, HTN, DM II who presented with 
malignant hypercalcemia, hyperglycemia, and an acute kidney 
injury after being discharged two days prior for the same issue. 


#Malignant hypercalcemia:
Pt presented to clinic and was found to have a calcium of 11.8. 
Of note, he was discharged only two days prior to admission for 
the same issue. His hypercalcemia is likely secondary to his 
multiple myeloma exacerbated by dehydration in the setting of 
osmotic diuresis from hyperglycemia. He was treated with fluids, 
and given bortezomib, dexamethasone 20 mg daily for 4 days, and 
cyclophosphamide with normalization of his calcium. He was 
scheduled to follow up with Dr. ___ primary 
hematologist, the day after discharge.

#Hyperglycemia:
Pt with history of uncontrolled DMII, followed by ___ as an 
outpatient. His hyperglycemia is likely due to his dexamethasone 
therapy as part of his multiple myeloma treatment, in addition 
to inconsistent adherence to his diabetes treatment plan. 
Initially, he required an insulin drip, however after 
consultation with ___ he was able to be transitioned to 
Lantus and a sliding scale. After some adjustment, his sugars 
were reasonably well-controlled. He was instructed to check his 
blood sugars four times daily and to follow up with his 
endocrinologist after discharge.

#HCAP Pneumonia:
During his course, he c/o a new cough, and a CXR revealed a left 
middle lung consolidation c/f pneumonia. He was initially 
started on azithromycin, however experienced a transaminitis so 
was transitioned to Levofloxacin. He remained afebrile with good 
oxygen saturations. He was discharged to complete a total of 8 
days of antibiotics.

___ on CKD: Pt initially noted in clinic  have a creatinine of 
1.9 up from a baseline of 1.1-1.2. Cr elevation likely from 
osmotic diuresis in setting of hyperglycemia, although likely 
contribution from advancing multiple myeloma as well. He was 
treated with aggressive fluid resuscitation with normalization 
of his creatinine.

Transaminitis: 
Patient experienced a transaminitis after receiving 
azithromycin. Abx were switched to levofloxacin with improvement 
in LFTs, although his ALT remained elevated at 47 at discharge.

# Refractory IgA Lambda Multiple Myeloma: Disease appears to be 
advancing despite previous autologous transplant and several 
chemotherapy regimens. While inpatient, patient received cycle 2 
of bortezomib and dexamethasone, this time with cyclophosphamide 
added. He was continued on acyclovir and Bactrim DS for 
prophylaxis and was scheduled to follow up with Dr. ___, 
___ hematologist, the day after discharge. 

# Hx of PE: Not on anticoagulation due to thrombocytopenia; 
underwent V/Q scan on ___ (prior admission) after experiencing 
DOE which showed a low likelihood of PE. Pt maintained good 
oxygen saturations and did not report any chest pain.

# Hx of hepatitis B infection:
- Continued home lamivudine

# Hypertension: 
- Continued diltiazem, carvedilol, amlodipine

# C difficile infection
- Continued vancomycin 125 mg PO q6h

# Gout: continued allopurinol

# Insomnia: Continued amitriptyline 25 mg po QHS
